```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(RDML)
```

## Tabular interfaces

Use `asTable()` and `getFData()` to move from the hierarchical S7 model to
ordinary tabular data.

```r
x <- rdmlRead("experiment.rdml")

metadata <- asTable(x)
curves <- getFData(
  x,
  dpType = "adp",
  longTable = TRUE
)
```

Both are `data.table` objects and can be converted with `as.data.frame()`.

## dplyr

```r
library(dplyr)

selected <- asTable(x) |>
  filter(sampleType == "std", adp)

curves <- getFData(
  x,
  request = selected,
  dpType = "adp",
  longTable = TRUE
)
```

## ggplot2

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(curves, aes(cyc, fluor, group = fdataName, colour = target)) +
  geom_line()
```

For melting curves use `dpType = "mdp"` and plot `tmp` against `fluor`.

## Wide data

Packages that expect one coordinate column plus one column per curve can use
wide output:

```r
wide <- getFData(
  x,
  dpType = "adp",
  longTable = FALSE
)

wide <- as.data.frame(wide)
```

This representation can be passed to `chipPCR`, `qpcR`, or custom analysis
functions after any preprocessing required by those packages.

## Writing calculated results back

Add result columns to a description table before calling `setFData()`.

```r
description <- asTable(x)
description$cq <- calculatedCq

x <- setFData(
  x,
  wide,
  description,
  fdataType = "adp",
  conflict = "keep"
)
```

For a completely new object use `rdmlFromFData()`.

## Select the curve type explicitly

Objects can contain amplification and melting curves simultaneously.

```r
amp <- getFData(x, dpType = "adp", longTable = TRUE)
melt <- getFData(x, dpType = "mdp", longTable = TRUE)
```

When only actual curves should be present in long output, filter the request
table by `adp` or `mdp` first.
